tips.title: Aligning Multi-Part Gun Barrels with Trumpeter & AFV Club
tips.text: Carefully dry-fit Trumpeter or AFV Club multi-part gun barrels. Apply a tiny drop of Tamiya Extra Thin Cement onto the joint, immediately slide the parts together, and hold until set. Repeat for each section, ensuring alignment. For complex barrels, use a jig from Clear Prop Models to maintain consistency.

tips.title: Installing Eduard Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: Before bending Eduard photo-etch parts, score them with a sharp knife along the bend lines. Use a GodHand nipper to carefully bend at these lines. For small, intricate parts, use a jeweler's bending tool. Attach parts using super glue — apply a small drop onto the part's edge, not the model's surface. Hold until set.

tips.title: Wing Alignment with a Simple Jig
tips.text: For multi-engine aircraft like the ICM P-51D, align wings using a simple jig. Cut a strip of cardboard to the wing's chord length. Tape it along the wing root rib, then lay the second wing on top, aligning its leading and trailing edges. Glue with Tamiya Extra Thin Cement, holding until set. Remove the jig after curing.

tips.title: Assembling Resin Conversion Kits
tips.text: With resin kits like Meng's conversion sets, cut parts carefully with a jeweler's saw or sharp knife. Clean up with 200 grit sandpaper, then use Tamiya Basic Cement to assemble, applying sparingly. For small parts, use CA glue. Let cure for 24 hours before handling. Fill gaps with Vallejo Plastic Putty.

tips.title: Strengthening Thin Parts with Brass Rod
tips.text: Reinforce thin parts like engine cowlings or gun bay doors using brass rod from Evergreen. Cut to length, drill a hole into the part with a 0.5mm drill bit. Insert the brass rod, securing it with super glue. Trim excess rod with a fine nippers. Drill and insert brass rod into both sides for added strength.
